Temporal happiness (by which he really seems to mean the lack of pain), may very well be a distraction to man insofar as it keeps his eyes away from God, Who is the true highest good and the salvation from all evil. Thus what Mackie calls "first order evil", or what I would just call suffering, is something that does not bring about a lesser order of good than that which the suffering interferes with, but in fact it brings about the true highest order of good, namely union with God. He then errs by suggesting the possibility of an infinite regress, that there might be some third order evil to contrast with the third order good. But if the third order good is said to be God (I'll just call it the highest order of good, no matter how many orders there are in between), upon reaching this order we reach the point where no evil can contrast it, because there is no privation in God. The infinite regress is stopped, and the existence of all the lesser orders of evil and understood within the context of this highest order.

Nor does this mean that suffering is necessary in itself, since, for one, it does not exist in itself, being only a privation of some due good; and secondly, because man chooses suffering when he chooses a lesser good to which evil is accidentally attached, rather than the Ultimate Good to which no evil is attached; and thirdly because man can accept suffering willingly for the sake of good. Love is sacrifice - because what we have to sacrifice is lesser than what we have to gain.
